subject: Post-demo: data access ledger & compliance evidence request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lara Bennett <lara@brightlinehealth.com>, procurement@brightlinehealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: data access ledger & compliance evidence request

Thanks again for your time today — really appreciated the deep dive into BrightLine's regulatory needs. Quick recap from our call and a proposed set of next steps so we can scope the evidence pack you asked about.

Key requirements I captured:
- PII classification: you need to confirm which fields are PII and how they map to BrightLine IDs vs. end-user identifiers.
- Auditability: exportable access logs that show who accessed a record, what resource was accessed, action (read/write/export), timestamp, and the requesting client IP or session id.
- Retention & exports: retention window of 3 years for audit logs, plus the ability to produce exports for a specific time range in CSV/JSON/Parquet formats.
- Residency: primary data residency in the us-east-1 region; logs must be available within the same legal boundary.
- Evidence format: PDF summary of controls (SOC2-style), raw log samples, and a data flow diagram linking identities to access events.

What we can provide immediately:
1) Sample access ledger export (synthetic) in CSV and ndjson formats — includes columns: timestamp, user_id, internal_user, action, resource_path, request_id, client_ip.
2) SOC2 summary (high level) and a one-page data flow diagram showing where logs are captured and stored.
3) Notes on RBAC, SSO mapping (SAML/OIDC), and KMS usage for encryption-at-rest keys.

Questions for you (so we scope the deliverables correctly):
- Can you confirm the canonical identifier BrightLine wants in the ledger (brightline_user_id vs email)?
- Do you need per-tenant separation in log exports, or will a filtering parameter be sufficient?
- Any regulatory artifacts beyond SOC2 that you'd like (HIPAA, ISO27001)?

Proposed next steps & timeline:
- Today: Ben to send synthetic ledger sample + SOC2 summary + data flow diagram (attached).
- Tue (05/05): Provide a filtered export for the last 90 days on request and a short write-up on retention policy and deletion workflows.
- Wed (05/06): Follow-up call with your IT Security team to walk through mapping and any redline requests.

Attachments: access_ledger_sample.csv (synthetic), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, data_flow_diagram.png

If that aligns, we'll get the sample files to you by EOD and set up the follow-up with Connor for Wed.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: access_ledger_sample.csv (CSV, 42KB), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF, 120KB), data_flow_diagram.png (PNG, 240KB)

From: Lara Bennett <lara@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlinehealth.com, IT Security <it-security@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 16:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: data access ledger & compliance evidence request

Ben — really helpful recap, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For the ledger canonical id we prefer brightline_user_id (internal MRN-like id) rather than email. We can provide a mapping table but would prefer the logs reference that ID for PHI minimization.
- Per-tenant separation: filtering is fine, but exports must be exportable by tenant-id and include a tenant_id column.
- Regulatory: HIPAA is required; if you can add any HIPAA-specific controls or mapping notes to the SOC2 summary that would be great.

On evidence — the compliance team needs: 
1) A 90-day export (sample) showing read/read_export events for at least 3 different users across two services.
2) A CSV and an ndjson sample; if Parquet is supported that's a plus for our analytics team.
3) A short write-up (1 page) explaining how Redwood correlates console/admin activity with API calls and how identities are resolved (SSO subject vs internal user id).

Time sensitivity: procurement wants the deliverables by EOD Tue to include in our vendor packet for next-week sign-off. Is that still achievable?

Thanks — looping in IT Security (it-security@brightlinehealth.com) to keep them in the loop.

—Lara
Lara Bennett
Head of IT Compliance | BrightLine Health

Hi Lara — we can absolutely meet the Tue EOD ask, here's how we'll scope the deliverables and a couple of follow-up questions.

Deliverables (proposed):
- 90-day filtered ledger export: CSV + ndjson (synthetic ids, redacted PII) — includes columns: tenant_id, brightline_user_id, timestamp, action, resource_path, request_id, client_ip, actor_type (api_key|user|service), resolved_identity (saml_subject if available).
- Parquet export: we can run a parquet export as an optional add-on; will include schema file.
- Controls summary: SOC2 high-level + HIPAA mapping page (1-page) + data flow diagram (attached).
- Identity correlation notes: short doc explaining how SSO subjects, API keys, and service accounts map to access events.

Questions for scope:
1) For the 90-day sample, should we synthesize the brightline_user_id mapping or would you prefer we accept a mapping table from you to replace our synthetic ids?
2) Any specific retention proof artifact you want (e.g., retention policy text, automated retention job logs, or proof of deletion events)?

Timeline:
- Today (Mon EOD): Ben will drop the synthetic CSV + SOC2 summary + data flow PNG.
- Tue morning: We will prepare the filtered 90-day CSV + ndjson and send by Tue EOD. If you want Parquet we'll need an extra business day.
- Wed: 30-minute walkthrough with Connor to validate identity mapping.

We'll attach the initial stubs now; Ben can push the sample ledger to the secure share.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
